title: Italy's data protection authority temporarily bans ChatGPT over GDPR violations
description: On 30 March 2023, Italy's Garante per la protezione dei dati personali ordered OpenAI to immediately stop processing Italian users' personal data, citing a lack of legal basis for the large-scale data collection used to train ChatGPT, the absence of age-verification mechanisms, and a recent data breach exposing user chat titles and payment information. Italy became the first Western country to block a major generative AI chatbot. After OpenAI implemented requested changes — including a privacy notice, an opt-out for training data, and an age-verification gate — the Garante lifted the restriction the following month.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty. Exact ban-lift date (commonly reported as 28 April 2023) drawn from secondary reporting rather than a directly confirmed primary Garante document.

organizations_involved: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
root_cause: OpenAI processed large volumes of personal data — scraped for training and generated through user conversations — without an adequate legal basis under GDPR, lacked transparency/privacy notices for EU users, and had no effective age-verification despite the service being usable by minors.

citations.title: Intelligenza artificiale: il Garante blocca ChatGPT. Raccolta illecita di dati personali. Assenza di sistemi per la verifica dell'età dei minori
citations.publisher: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali

relationships.reason: A documented GDPR legal basis and age-verification gate before EU launch addresses exactly the deficiencies the Garante identified.
This is the first, and most prominent, regulator action of its kind against a consumer generative AI product.
